record.name: Uruguay
record.summary: No qualifying institute identified. A national AI research centre, Instituto Vidart, opened in September 2026 without an evaluation mandate, and the digital government agency AGESIC is considering an AI profile for the national cybersecurity framework.

next_check.reason: Routine re-check on a two-year rotation of states with no reported plans.

English searches for a national AI safety, security or evaluation institute, commitment, proposal or study. English results concern Instituto Vidart, AI research and national cybersecurity governance. The cached government launch account gives Vidart research, talent and technology-transfer functions. No separate AISI commitment or new mandate to evaluate advanced models for severe risks was identified. Partial check only; the last full-check date is unchanged.

check.independence_note: Historical audit under the superseded two-independent-sources rule: Two substantively independent evidence origins were not established. Multiple pages from one owner, mirrors, reports of the same underlying announcement and general regional coverage are not counted as independent corroboration.
check.governance_note: The government launch account describes the Vidart national AI centre and its research role, rather than an identified mandate to evaluate the safety of advanced models.

related_bodies.name: AGESIC
related_bodies.role: As of June 2026, it was studying an AI profile for the cybersecurity framework and had not updated its guidance. It is a digital government agency. It is not an evaluation institute.

related_bodies.name: Instituto Vidart (Centro Nacional de Inteligencia Artificial)
related_bodies.role: Its research lines include safety and explainability. It is a national AI research centre launched on 7 September 2026 by Uruguay Innova, SENCI and AGESIC. It has no evaluation or audit mandate.

record.notes: AGESIC details rest on one secondary article; the Vidart launch is from the government's own announcement.
